newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says German coalition backs new budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says German coalition backs new budget cuts.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday Germany's governing coalition had agreed to new budget cuts that would hold the level of new debt in 1997 to under 56.5 billion marks ($38 billion).

Waigel told journalists that the entire coalition had approved an agreement hammered out late on Sunday by leaders of the coalition partners -- the Christian Democrats (CDU/CSU) and the liberal Free Democrats (FDP).

He got his way on Sunday night when coalition leaders approved three billion marks ($2 billion) in savings after feuding which at one point had provoked Chancellor Helmut Kohl to threaten to quit after 14 years in power.
A billion marks will come out of the Federal Labour Office budget.
Waigel's other cuts will come from Defence (200 million marks), Transport (450 million), Economics (260 million), and Research (160 million) with smaller savings being spread over other ministries.
Waigel said the total federal spending in 1997 would be 440 billion marks ($293 billion).
